# useState — derived vs duplicated state

> A copied selection and a stored total drift out of sync; storing an id and deriving the rest fixes both.

🟡 intermediate · React 16.8+ · Built-in Hooks › State & context · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-state-derived-state`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-state-derived-state)

## Concept

Keep the _minimal_ state and compute everything else during render. Store `selectedId`, not a copy of the selected object; compute totals and filtered lists from the source array.

## Problem

Duplicated state has to be updated in every code path that changes the original. Miss one and the UI shows contradictory data — the demo renames an item but the "selected" label keeps the old name.

## When to use

- Whenever a value can be computed from props or other state.
- Selections: store ids/indexes; look the object up during render.

## When not to use

- Intentionally frozen snapshots (an "initial value" prop, a form's original values for a reset) — name them `initialX` to make that explicit.

## API

```ts
const selected = items.find((item) => item.id === selectedId); // derived
```

## Execution flow

1. Render reads the source state (`items`, `selectedId`).
2. Derived values are plain expressions in the component body, recomputed every render.
3. Only if profiling shows a cost, wrap the computation in `useMemo`.

## Common mistakes

### Copying an item into state

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(items[0]);
```

Editing `items` does not update the copy, so the selection shows stale data.

✅ Correct:

```tsx
const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(items[0].id);
const selectedItem = items.find((item) => item.id === selectedId);
```

### Syncing derived values with an effect

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  setTotal(items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0));
}, [items]);
```

Renders once with a stale total, then again with the right one — and is easy to forget.

✅ Correct:

```tsx
const total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0);
```

## Edge cases

- When the selected item is deleted, the derived lookup returns `undefined` — handle it in render instead of resetting state in an effect.

## Testing

The demo test renames the selected item and changes a price in both panels, asserting the duplicated panel is stale while the derived panel is correct.

- [`src/examples/built-in/state/UseStateDerivedStateDemo.test.tsx`](../../src/examples/built-in/state/UseStateDerivedStateDemo.test.tsx)

## Production considerations

- Normalise collections (`byId` + `ids`) when many places select by id.
- For expensive derivations, `useMemo` (or the React Compiler) caches without duplicating state.
